one_line: Personified spirit of early Kadamba temple towers, a young Deccan architect-priest shaping the first stepped shikharas over square sanctums.

appearance.age_look: mid-20s, lean and wiry with the build of a field architect used to climbing scaffolds and hauling stone models
appearance.face: oval face with a warm medium-brown Deccan complexion, straight nose, sharp jawline, slightly arched brows, large focused anime-style eyes with dark irises, a small tilak of white vertical paste on the forehead, default expression calm and observant with a faint, thoughtful half-smile as if visualising elevations in his mind
appearance.hair: thick black hair parted softly in the middle, drawn back into a neat low knotted bun at the nape (architect’s practicality), a few shorter strands loose at the temples; he wears a narrow off-white cotton headband tied around the forehead, its knot hidden at the back under the bun
appearance.costume: simple early-Deccan temple-architect attire: an unbleached off-white cotton angavastra draped over both shoulders and wrapped securely around the torso like a modest upper cloth, paired with a knee-length dull-ochre cotton dhoti wrapped tightly and pleated in front, the ends reaching mid-calf; the dhoti is bordered with a thin dark-red line; he has a plain brown leather belt-like cloth sash at the waist from which hangs a small cloth pouch; around his neck is a single strand of tulasi-like wooden beads; his wrists bear two thin copper bangles; he is barefoot but with sturdy calloused feet, an anklet of simple iron rings on his right ankle; the fabrics are matte, slightly worn, and practical for site work, with no heavy ornamentation, evoking a modest brahmin-architect moving between Halasi and Talagunda
appearance.signature: a palm-sized wooden miniature model of a square sanctum topped with a stepped Kadamba shikhara – four clean horizontal tiers and a simple rounded finial – which he usually cradles in one hand while the other holds a short measuring cord and a small iron chisel tucked into his waist sash

ref_desc: Kadamba Shikhara is a medium-brown, oval-faced young man with large focused eyes, black hair in a low bun with an off-white headband, wearing an off-white angavastra, dull-ochre dhoti with dark-red border, simple beads and bangles, barefoot, carrying a wooden stepped-shikhara model and small tools in warm earthy colours.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character sheet of Kadamba Shikhara, the personified spirit of early Kadamba temple towers: a mid-20s, lean young man with an oval medium-brown Deccan face, straight nose, sharp jawline, slightly arched brows, large focused dark eyes and a small white vertical tilak, his default expression calm and observant with a faint thoughtful half-smile. His thick black hair is parted in the middle, pulled into a neat low bun at the nape, with a few loose strands at the temples, and a narrow off-white cotton headband tied around his forehead. He wears a historically plausible early-Deccan outfit: an unbleached off-white cotton angavastra draped over both shoulders and wrapped modestly around the torso, and a knee-length dull-ochre cotton dhoti with a thin dark-red border, tightly wrapped and pleated in front, reaching mid-calf. A plain brown cloth sash at his waist holds a small cloth pouch and an iron chisel; around his neck is a single strand of simple wooden beads, his wrists have thin copper bangles, and he is barefoot with a discreet iron anklet on his right ankle. In his right hand he cradles a palm-sized wooden model of a square sanctum topped with a stepped Kadamba shikhara tower of four horizontal tiers and a simple rounded finial, while his left hand lightly holds a short measuring cord, reinforcing his role as architect; render fabrics as matte, slightly worn cotton, and keep the palette in warm earthy tones of off-white, dull ochre, dark red, warm brown and matte copper, with clean, consistent design lines suitable for redrawing in many panels.
